item.title: Nagoya Women's Marathon: The World's Largest Women's Race — Guide
item.description: The Nagoya Women’s Marathon, run each year on a Sunday in early March, is recognised as the world’s largest women-only marathon, bringing some 20,000 runners from around the globe onto a flat, fast course that loops from Nagoya Dome past Nagoya Castle, the Sakae skyline and the city’s broad avenues. The race is famous for its finisher’s reward — an exclusive Tiffany & Co. pendant handed over by tuxedoed presenters — and for the city-wide festival mood, with cheering squads, taiko teams and a running expo that make marathon weekend one of Nagoya’s liveliest.

item.title: Hakone Ekiden Guide: New Year Relay Race & Access
item.description: Every January 2nd and 3rd, the nation stops to watch the Hakone Ekiden — the most beloved and dramatic long-distance relay race in Japan. University teams of runners carry a sash (tasuki) over a gruelling ~217 km round-trip course between Tokyo and Hakone, climbing the steep mountain road past Odawara to Lake Ashi and back. The race is a New Year institution, with millions watching on TV and huge crowds lining the route to cheer the young runners through cold, hills and exhaustion.

item.title: Naha Marathon Guide: Date, Course & Entry
item.description: The Naha Marathon is one of Japan’s most popular and warmly welcoming road races — a full marathon held each December under Okinawa’s mild winter skies. Tens of thousands of runners loop from central Naha through the southern part of the island, cheered on by legendary local support: residents line the route handing out snacks, awamori and high-fives in true Okinawan style. With a sub-tropical climate and festive atmosphere, it’s a bucket-list race for runners and a fun spectacle for visitors.
